title: Definition and notation of complex numbers
statement: Definition of complex numbers in the form $a + ib$ and $r\cos\theta + ir\sin\theta$.
guidance: The meaning of conjugate, modulus, argument, real part, imaginary part and equality of complex numbers should be known.

title: Sum, product and quotient of complex numbers
statement: Sum, product and quotient of complex numbers.
guidance: $|z_1 z_2| = |z_1||z_2|$. Knowledge of the result $\arg(z_1 z_2) = \arg z_1 + \arg z_2$ is not required.

title: Argand diagram representation of complex numbers
statement: Geometrical representation of complex numbers in the Argand diagram. Geometrical representation of sums, products and quotients of complex numbers.

title: Complex roots of quadratic equations
statement: Complex solutions of quadratic equations with real coefficients.

title: Conjugate roots of cubic equations
statement: Finding conjugate complex roots and a real root of a cubic equation with integer coefficients.
guidance: Knowledge that if $z_1$ is a root of $f(z) = 0$ then $z_1^*$ is also a root.

title: Conjugate roots of quartic equations
statement: Finding conjugate complex roots and/or real roots of a quartic equation with real coefficients.
guidance: For example, (i) $f(x) = x^4 - x^3 - 5x^2 + 7x + 10$. Given that $x = 2 + i$ is a root of $f(x) = 0$, use algebra to find the three other roots of $f(x) = 0$. (ii) $g(x) = x^4 - x^3 + 6x^2 + 14x - 20$. Given $g(1) = 0$ and $g(-2) = 0$, use algebra to solve $g(x) = 0$ completely.

title: Sum and product of quadratic roots
statement: Sum of roots and product of roots of a quadratic equation.
guidance: For the equation $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$, whose roots are $\alpha$ and $\beta$, $\alpha + \beta = -\dfrac{b}{a}$, $\alpha\beta = \dfrac{c}{a}$.

title: Manipulating symmetric root expressions
statement: Manipulation of expressions involving the sum of roots and product of roots.
guidance: Knowledge of the identity $\alpha^3 + \beta^3 \equiv (\alpha+\beta)^3 - 3\alpha\beta(\alpha+\beta)$.

title: Forming quadratics with transformed roots
statement: Forming quadratic equations with new roots.
glossary: sum and product of new roots
guidance: For example, with roots $\alpha^3, \beta^3$; $\dfrac{1}{\alpha}, \dfrac{1}{\beta}$; $\alpha + \dfrac{2}{\alpha}, \beta + \dfrac{2}{\beta}$; etc.

title: Numerical solution of equations
statement: Equations of the form $f(x) = 0$ solved numerically by: (i) interval bisection, (ii) linear interpolation, (iii) the Newton-Raphson process.
guidance: $f(x)$ will involve only functions used in P1 and P2. For the Newton-Raphson process, the only differentiation required will be as defined in unit P1 and P2.

title: Parabola and rectangular hyperbola equations
statement: Cartesian equations for the parabola and rectangular hyperbola.
guidance: Students should be familiar with the equations: $y^2 = 4ax$ or $x = at^2, y = 2at$ and $xy = c^2$ or $x = ct, y = \dfrac{c}{t}$.

title: Parametric point on the parabola
statement: Idea of parametric equation for parabola and rectangular hyperbola.
guidance: The idea of $(at^2, 2at)$ as a general point on the parabola is all that is required.

title: Focus-directrix property of the parabola
statement: The focus-directrix property of the parabola.
guidance: Concept of focus and directrix and parabola as locus of points equidistant from focus and directrix.

title: Tangents and normals to these curves
statement: Tangents and normals to these curves.
guidance: Differentiation of $y^2 = 4ax$ to give $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2a}{y}$, and of $xy = c^2$ to give $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{c^2}{x^2}$. Parametric differentiation is not required.

title: Addition and subtraction of matrices
statement: Addition and subtraction of matrices.

title: Scalar multiplication of a matrix
statement: Multiplication of a matrix by a scalar.

title: Multiplying matrices together
statement: Products of matrices.

title: Evaluating 2x2 determinants
statement: Evaluation of $2 \times 2$ determinants.
guidance: Singular and non-singular matrices.

title: Inverse of 2x2 matrices
statement: Inverse of $2 \times 2$ matrices.
guidance: Use of the relation $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$.

title: Matrix representation of linear transformations
statement: Linear transformations of column vectors in two dimensions and their matrix representation.
guidance: The transformation represented by $AB$ is the transformation represented by $B$ followed by the transformation represented by $A$.

title: Matrices for geometric transformations
statement: Applications of $2 \times 2$ matrices to represent geometrical transformations.
guidance: Identification and use of the matrix representation of single transformations from: reflection in coordinate axes and lines $y = \pm x$; rotation through any angle about $(0,0)$; stretches parallel to the $x$-axis and $y$-axis; and enlargement about centre $(0,0)$ with scale factor $k$ ($k \neq 0$), where $k \in \mathbb{R}$.

title: Combining matrix transformations
statement: Combinations of transformations.
guidance: Identification and use of the matrix representation of combined transformations.

title: Inverse of combined transformations
statement: The inverse (when it exists) of a given transformation or combination of transformations.
guidance: Idea of the determinant as an area scale factor in transformations.

title: Summing simple finite series
statement: Summation of simple finite series.
guidance: Students should be able to sum series such as $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n} r^2$, $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n} r^3$ and $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n} r(r+2)$. The method of differences is not required.

title: Proof by mathematical induction
statement: Proof by mathematical induction.
guidance: To include induction proofs for (i) summation of series, e.g. show $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^n r^3 = \dfrac{1}{4}n^2(n+1)^2$ or $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^n r(r+1) = \dfrac{1}{3}n(n+1)(n+2)$ (ii) divisibility, e.g. show $3^{2n+1} + 1$ is divisible by 4 (iii) finding general terms in a sequence, e.g. if $u_{n+1} = 3u_n + 4$ with $u_1 = 1$, prove that $u_n = 3^n - 2$ (iv) matrix products, e.g. show that $A^n$ for a given $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ can be found in terms of $n$.

title: Solving algebraic and modulus inequalities
statement: The manipulation and solution of algebraic inequalities and inequations, including those involving the modulus sign.
guidance: The solution of inequalities such as $\dfrac{1}{x} > x$, $|x^2 - 1| > 2(x+1)$ and $\dfrac{1}{x-a} > \dfrac{1}{x-b}$.

title: Method of differences for series
statement: Summation of simple finite series using the method of differences.
guidance: Students should be able to sum series such as $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n} \dfrac{1}{r(r+1)}$ using partial fractions such as $\dfrac{1}{r(r+1)} = \dfrac{1}{r} - \dfrac{1}{r+1}$.

title: Euler's relation for complex exponentials
statement: Euler's relation $e^{i\theta} = \cos\theta + i\sin\theta$.
guidance: Students should be familiar with $\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}(e^{i\theta} + e^{-i\theta})$ and $\sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{2i}(e^{i\theta} - e^{-i\theta})$.

title: De Moivre's theorem and applications
statement: De Moivre's theorem and its application to trigonometric identities and to roots of a complex number.
glossary: nth roots of a complex number
guidance: To include finding $\cos n\theta$ and $\sin n\theta$ in terms of powers of $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$ and also powers of $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$ in terms of multiple angles. Students should be able to prove De Moivre's theorem for any integer $n$.

title: Loci and regions in Argand diagram
statement: Loci and regions in the Argand diagram.
guidance: Loci such as $|z-a| = b$, $|z-a| = k|z-b|$, $\arg(z-a) = \beta$, $\arg\left(\dfrac{z-a}{z-b}\right) = \beta$, and regions such as $|z-a| \leqslant |z-b|$ and $|z-a| \leqslant b$.

title: Transformations from z-plane to w-plane
statement: Elementary transformations from the $z$-plane to the $w$-plane.
guidance: Transformations such as $w = z^2$ and $w = \dfrac{az+b}{cz+d}$, where $a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{C}$, may be set.

title: Separable first order differential equations
statement: Further solution of first order differential equations with separable variables.
guidance: The formation of the differential equation may be required. Students will be expected to obtain particular solutions and also sketch members of the family of solution curves.

title: Linear first order differential equations
statement: First order linear differential equations of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q$ where $P$ and $Q$ are functions of $x$.
glossary: e to the integral of p dx
guidance: The integrating factor $e^{\int P \, dx}$ may be quoted without proof.

title: Differential equations reducible by substitution
statement: Differential equations reducible to the above types by means of a given substitution.

title: Second order linear differential equations
statement: The linear second order differential equation $a\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + b\dfrac{dy}{dx} + cy = f(x)$ where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are real constants and the particular integral can be found by inspection or trial.
guidance: The auxiliary equation may have real distinct, equal or complex roots. $f(x)$ will have one of the forms $ke^{px}$, $A + Bx$, $p + qx + cx^2$ or $m\cos\omega x + n\sin\omega x$. Students should be familiar with the terms 'complementary function' and 'particular integral'. Students should be able to solve equations of the form $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 4y = \sin 2x$.

title: Second order DEs reducible by substitution
statement: Differential equations reducible to the above types by means of a given substitution.

title: Third and higher order derivatives
statement: Third and higher order derivatives.

title: Maclaurin series derivation and use
statement: Derivation and use of Maclaurin series.
guidance: The derivation of the series expansion of $e^x$, $\sin x$, $\cos x$, $\ln(1+x)$ and other simple functions may be required.

title: Taylor series derivation and use
statement: Derivation and use of Taylor series.
guidance: The derivation, for example, of the expansion of $\sin x$ in ascending powers of $(x - \pi)$ up to and including the term in $(x-\pi)^3$.

title: Series solutions of differential equations
statement: Use of Taylor series method for series solutions of differential equations.
guidance: Students may, for example, be required to find the solution in powers of $x$ as far as the term in $x^4$, of the differential equation $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 0$, such that $y = 1$, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$ at $x = 0$.

title: Polar coordinates and curve sketching
statement: Polar coordinates $(r, \theta)$, $r \geqslant 0$.
guidance: The sketching of curves such as $\theta = \alpha$, $r = p\sec(\alpha - \theta)$, $r = a$, $r = 2a\cos\theta$, $r = k\theta$, $r = a(1 \pm \cos\theta)$, $r = a(3 + 2\cos\theta)$, $r = a\cos 2\theta$ and $r^2 = a^2\cos 2\theta$ may be set.

title: Area enclosed by a polar curve
statement: Use of the formula $\dfrac{1}{2}\displaystyle\int_{\alpha}^{\beta} r^2 \, d\theta$ for area.
guidance: The ability to find tangents parallel to, or at right angles to, the initial line is expected.

title: Definitions and identities of hyperbolic functions
statement: Definition of the six hyperbolic functions in terms of exponentials. Graphs and properties of the hyperbolic functions.
guidance: For example, $\cosh x = \dfrac{1}{2}(e^x + e^{-x})$, $\operatorname{sech} x = \dfrac{1}{\cosh x} = \dfrac{2}{e^x + e^{-x}}$. Students should be able to derive and use simple identities such as $\cosh^2 x - \sinh^2 x \equiv 1$ and $\cosh^2 x + \sinh^2 x \equiv \cosh 2x$ and to solve equations such as $a\cosh x + b\sinh x = c$.

title: Inverse hyperbolic functions and logarithmic forms
statement: Inverse hyperbolic functions, their graphs, properties and logarithmic equivalents.
guidance: For example, $\operatorname{arsinh} x = \ln\left(x + \sqrt{1+x^2}\right)$. Students may be required to prove this and similar results.

title: Ellipse and hyperbola equations
statement: Cartesian and parametric equations for the ellipse and hyperbola.
guidance: Extension of work from FP1. Students should be familiar with the equations: $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$; $x = a\cos t, y = b\sin t$. $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$; $x = a\sec t, y = b\tan t$; $x = a\cosh t, y = b\sinh t$.

title: Focus-directrix properties of ellipse and hyperbola
statement: The focus-directrix properties of the ellipse and hyperbola, including the eccentricity.
guidance: For example, students should know that, for the ellipse, $b^2 = a^2(1-e^2)$, the foci are $(ae, 0)$ and $(-ae, 0)$ and the equations of the directrices are $x = \dfrac{a}{e}$ and $x = -\dfrac{a}{e}$.

title: Tangents and normals to ellipse and hyperbola
statement: Tangents and normals to these curves.
guidance: The condition for $y = mx + c$ to be a tangent to these curves is expected to be known.

title: Loci problems with conics
statement: Simple loci problems.

title: Differentiating hyperbolic function expressions
statement: Differentiation of hyperbolic functions and expressions involving them.
guidance: For example, $\tanh 3x$, $x\sinh^2 x$, $\dfrac{\cosh 2x}{(x+1)^2}$.

title: Differentiating inverse trig and hyperbolic functions
statement: Differentiation of inverse functions, including trigonometric and hyperbolic functions.
guidance: For example, $\arcsin x + \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$, $\dfrac{1}{2}\operatorname{artanh}(x^2)$.

title: Integrating hyperbolic function expressions
statement: Integration of hyperbolic functions and expressions involving them.

title: Integrating inverse trig and hyperbolic functions
statement: Integration of inverse trigonometric and hyperbolic functions.
guidance: For example, $\displaystyle\int \operatorname{arsinh} x \, dx$, $\displaystyle\int \arctan x \, dx$.

title: Hyperbolic and trigonometric substitution integrals
statement: Integration using hyperbolic and trigonometric substitutions.
guidance: To include the integrals of $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a^2+x^2}}$, $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a^2-x^2}}$, $\dfrac{1}{a^2+x^2}$ and $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^2-a^2}}$.

title: Integrals involving quadratic surds
statement: Use of substitution for integrals involving quadratic surds.
guidance: In more complicated cases, substitutions will be given.

title: Deriving reduction formulae for integrals
statement: The derivation and use of simple reduction formulae.
guidance: Students should be able to derive formulae such as $nI_n = (n-1)I_{n-2}$, $n \geqslant 2$, for $I_n = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \sin^n x \, dx$, and $I_n = I_{n-2} + \dfrac{2\sin((n-1)x)}{n-1}$ for $I_n = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{\sin nx}{\sin x} \, dx$, $n > 0$.

title: Arc length and surface of revolution
statement: The calculation of arc length and the area of a surface of revolution.
guidance: The equation of the curve may be given in Cartesian or parametric form. Equations in polar form will not be set.

title: Vector product and triple scalar product
statement: The vector product $\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}$ and the triple scalar product $\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c}$.
guidance: The interpretation of $|\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}|$ as an area and $\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c}$ as a volume.

title: Vector equations of lines and planes
statement: Use of vectors in problems involving points, lines and planes. The equation of a line in the form $(\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{a}) \times \mathbf{b} = \mathbf{0}$.
guidance: Students may be required to use equivalent Cartesian forms also. Applications to include (i) distance from a point to a plane, (ii) line of intersection of two planes, (iii) shortest distance between two skew lines.

title: Vector and cartesian equations of planes
statement: The equation of a plane in the forms $\mathbf{r} \cdot \mathbf{n} = p$, $\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{a} + s\mathbf{b} + t\mathbf{c}$.
guidance: Students may be required to use equivalent Cartesian forms also.

title: Matrix transformations in three dimensions
statement: Linear transformations of column vectors in two and three dimensions and their matrix representation.
guidance: Extension of work from FP1 to 3 dimensions.

title: Combining 3D matrix transformations
statement: Combination of transformations. Products of matrices.
guidance: The transformation represented by $AB$ is the transformation represented by $B$ followed by the transformation represented by $A$.

title: Transpose of a matrix
statement: Transpose of a matrix.
guidance: Use of the relation $(AB)^T = B^T A^T$.

title: Evaluating 3x3 determinants
statement: Evaluation of $3 \times 3$ determinants.
guidance: Singular and non-singular matrices.

title: Inverse of 3x3 matrices
statement: Inverse of $3 \times 3$ matrices.
guidance: Use of the relation $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$.

title: Inverse of 3D transformations
statement: The inverse (when it exists) of a given transformation or combination of transformations.

title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of matrices
statement: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of $2 \times 2$ and $3 \times 3$ matrices.
guidance: Normalised vectors may be required.

title: Diagonalising symmetric matrices
statement: Reduction of symmetric matrices to diagonal form.
guidance: Students should be able to find an orthogonal matrix $P$ such that $P^TAP$ is diagonal.
